column5: For a CM field E of degree 2g: a set Phi of g complex embeddings of E containing exactly one of each pair of complex conjugate embeddings. In the Lean source it is a choice of one embedding Phi_tau for each infinite place tau of E (class CMType); for E = K(zeta) all Phi_tau restrict to the fixed inclusion of K in C and Phi_tau = Phi_1 composed with an element of Gal(E/K).
column6: CM field; complex embedding of a number field; infinite place of a number field

column5: A totally imaginary quadratic extension of a totally real number field. Complex conjugation induces the same automorphism under every complex embedding. Here E = K(zeta), K = Q(sqrt(-d)), zeta a primitive q1-th root of unity.
column6: number field; totally real number field; complex embedding of a number field

column5: The monic polynomial Phi_n whose roots are the primitive n-th roots of unity; degree phi(n). Used: Phi_n(X) = Phi_m(X^(n/m)) when every prime of n divides m; over K = Q(sqrt(-d)) with gcd(n, d) = 1 and the conditions of the parameters Phi_{q1} is irreducible.
column6: primitive root of unity; Euler totient function

column5: For an extension L/K of number fields the different D_{L/K} is the inverse of the fractional ideal {x in L : Tr_{L/K}(x O_L) contained in O_K} (the codifferent). If O_L = O_K[a] with minimal polynomial f then D_{L/K} = (f'(a)). Used for E/K with generator P'(zeta), P the q1-th cyclotomic polynomial.
column6: fractional ideal; field trace; ring of integers of a number field; codifferent

column5: If f_n -> f almost everywhere and |f_n| <= g with g integrable, then the integrals of f_n converge to the integral of f. Used in the series form: a series of functions whose norms are dominated termwise by a series with integrable sum can be integrated term by term.
column6: Lebesgue integral; integrable function

column1: Dual basis for the trace form
column5: For a finite separable extension L/K with basis b_1..b_n, the basis b_i* with Tr_{L/K}(b_i* b_j) = delta_ij. Euler's formula: if L = K(a) with minimal polynomial f and f(X)/(X - a) = sum c_i X^i, the dual basis of 1, a, ..., a^(n-1) is c_i / f'(a).
column6: field trace; separable extension; dual basis

column5: A function C -> C (or C^n -> C) that is holomorphic everywhere. Used: an entire function equals the sum of its Taylor series at 0, so it vanishes if the series does.
column6: holomorphic function

column5: gamma = lim (1 + 1/2 + ... + 1/n - log n). Occurs in the Chowla-Selberg constant gamma - Re L'/L(1, chi_K).
column6: harmonic number; natural logarithm

column5: If a_(m+n) <= a_m + a_n for a real sequence then a_n/n converges to inf a_n/n. Used in multiplicative form: for c_(m+n) <= c_m c_n with values in [0,1], c_0 = 1 and 0 < b <= 1, if b^q <= c_q for arbitrarily large q then b^n <= c_n for all n.
column6: subadditive sequence; limit of a sequence

column5: For a finite extension L/K, Tr_{L/K}(x) is the trace of multiplication by x as a K-linear map of L; for a Galois extension it is the sum of the conjugates of x.
column6: field extension; trace of a linear map

column1: Finite adele ring of a number field
column5: The restricted product of the completions E_w over the finite places w with respect to the valuation rings; its subring of integral adeles is the product of the valuation rings (written O-hat). E embeds diagonally with dense image. A unit is a finite idele.
column6: place of a global field; completion of a valued field; restricted product

column1: Frobenius coin problem for two coprime integers
column5: If a, b are coprime positive integers, every integer n >= (a-1)(b-1) is of the form xa + yb with natural numbers x, y.
column6: coprime integers; Bezout identity

column5: Every natural number is a sum of four squares of integers. Used to deduce by compactness that every p-adic integer is a sum of four squares of p-adic integers.
column6: natural number; square number

column5: For a prime p and n >= 0: v_p(n!) = sum_{i>=1} floor(n/p^i) = (n - s_p(n))/(p - 1), with s_p(n) the sum of the digits of n in base p. Consequences used: v_p(n!) = floor(n/p) + v_p(floor(n/p)!), v_p(n!) <= n/(p-1), and v_p(n!) >= n/(p-1) - D if n < p^D.
column6: p-adic valuation; factorial

column5: For a prime p and a nonzero integer n, v_p(n) is the largest e with p^e dividing n; extended to Q, Q_p and C_p by |x|_p = p^(-v_p(x)).
column6: prime number; divisibility

column5: An element z of a field with z^n = 1 and z^m != 1 for 0 < m < n. Its powers z^0..z^(n-1) are the n-th roots of unity and sum_{i<n} rho^i = 0 for an n-th root of unity rho != 1.
column6: root of unity; field

column1: Quadratic Dirichlet character of a quadratic field
column5: For K = Q(sqrt(-d)), d a prime = 3 mod 4: the character chi_K(n) = (n/d) (Legendre symbol), equal to 1, -1, 0 at a prime p that splits, is inert, ramifies in K; L(s, chi_K) is its Dirichlet L-function.
column6: Dirichlet character; Legendre symbol; quadratic number field; splitting of primes in an extension

column1: Ring of integers of a number field
column5: The integral closure of Z in a number field. For K = Q(sqrt(-d)), d = 3 mod 4: O_K = Z + Z (1 + sqrt(-d))/2, a lattice in C of covolume sqrt(d)/2.
column6: number field; integral closure

column5: For a number field E of degree n with discriminant d_E: rd_E = |d_E|^(1/n).
column6: discriminant of a number field

column5: Form used: a number field E is dense in its ring of finite adeles (equivalently E + O-hat = A_f; this is the Chinese remainder theorem for the Dedekind domain O_E).
column6: finite adele ring of a number field; Chinese remainder theorem; Dedekind domain

column5: For finitely many pairwise inequivalent absolute values of a field F, the diagonal image of F in the product of the completions is dense. Form used: the image of a CM field E under the embeddings of a CM type is dense in the product of copies of C over the infinite places.
column6: absolute value on a field; completion of a valued field; place of a global field

column5: For a power series F in variables X_i and power series a_i without constant term (in any variables), F(a) is the power series obtained by substituting a_i for X_i; it is a continuous ring homomorphism in F. Special cases: rescaling X_i -> c X_i and linear substitutions.
column6: formal power series ring; multivariable formal power series ring

column5: For a function f holomorphic near 0 in C: the formal power series sum_k f^(k)(0)/k! X^k. For entire f it converges to f everywhere; the Taylor series of a product is the product, and that of f(cz) is obtained by X -> cX.
column6: holomorphic function; formal power series ring; derivative

column5: C_p: the completion of an algebraic closure of Q_p for the unique extension of the p-adic absolute value, normalised by |p| = 1/p; complete, algebraically closed, ultrametric; valuation ring O = {|x| <= 1} with maximal ideal {|x| < 1}. A p-adic place of C in the Lean source is a ring homomorphism iota_p: C -> C_p (not assumed continuous).
column6: p-adic field; algebraic closure; completion of a valued field; non-Archimedean absolute value; valuation ring

column5: For a non-Archimedean absolute value: |x + y| <= max(|x|, |y|), with equality if |x| != |y|; hence a finite sum is bounded by the largest term and |1 + x| = 1 for |x| < 1.
column6: non-Archimedean absolute value

column5: For a lattice L in C: wp(z) = 1/z^2 + sum over nonzero w in L of (1/(z-w)^2 - 1/w^2), an even L-periodic meromorphic function with double poles at L. Used through the translated coordinates x(z) = wp(z+t) - wp(t) and y(z) = (wp'(z+t) - a_1 (wp(z+t) - wp(t)))/2 for a point t of order two and a_1^2 = 12 wp(t).
column6: lattice in the complex plane; meromorphic function; elliptic function

column5: For a lattice L in C: sigma(z) = z prod over nonzero w in L of (1 - z/w) exp(z/w + z^2/(2w^2)), an entire odd function with simple zeros exactly at L and (log sigma)'' = -wp. The theta function of a CM lattice in the Lean source is the twisted translate of sigma by the marked point t of order two, normalised to value 1 at 0.
column6: lattice in the complex plane; entire function; Weierstrass elliptic function

column5: A lattice L in C with a L contained in L for all a in the ring of integers of an imaginary quadratic field K. In the Lean source (CMLattice d) it comes with a marked point t of order two, is normalised at t, and has the hermitian form H(l, z) = (pi/A) conj(l) z, A the area of a period parallelogram.
column6: lattice in the complex plane; imaginary quadratic field; ring of integers of a number field

column5: Describes the action of automorphisms of C over K on a CM elliptic curve and its torsion points through ideles of K (Shimura, Introduction to the arithmetic theory of automorphic functions, Theorem 5.4). Form used: for sigma in Aut(C/K) there are a number Omega and a finite adele beta of K such that sigma maps the Taylor series of the theta function translated by x Omega_0 to that of the conjugate lattice translated by x' Omega for x' in K close to beta x; no reciprocity law is used.
column6: Lattice with complex multiplication; idele group; elliptic curve

column5: Expresses the periods of elliptic curves with complex multiplication by an imaginary quadratic field K through values of the Gamma function, equivalently through L'/L(1, chi_K). Form used: there is a number u, a unit at every p-adic place, with area(C^sigma) |sigma u|^2 = pi exp(gamma - Re L'/L(1, chi_K)) 2 pi / sqrt(d) for all conjugates C^sigma of the CM lattice.
column6: Lattice with complex multiplication; Dirichlet L-function; Euler–Mascheroni constant

column5: A power series F(X, Y) = X + Y + ... over a ring with F(X, F(Y, Z)) = F(F(X, Y), Z) and F(X, 0) = X. Used: the parameter y of a CM elliptic curve has an integral addition law, y(z0 + z1) is a power series in y(z0), y(z1) with p-integral coefficients.
column6: formal power series ring

column5: For a symplectic (or hermitian) space W over a ring: the central extension of W by the additive group with multiplication (w, t)(w', t') = (w + w', t + t' + <w, w'>/2). Its Schroedinger/Fock representation on a Schwartz space underlies the Weil representation; here adelic, with finite Heisenberg operators acting by translation times a character.
column6: symplectic form; central extension; adele ring of a number field

column5: The projective representation of the symplectic (here: unitary, via a splitting character) adelic group on the space of the Heisenberg representation, intertwining the Heisenberg action; its theta functional is the automorphic linear form summing over rational points.
column6: Heisenberg group; unitary group of a hermitian space; adele ring of a number field

column5: (n_1 + ... + n_k)! / (n_1! ... n_k!), a natural number.
column6: factorial

column5: For lattices L, L' in C a complex number a with a L contained in L'; its degree is the index [L' : a L]. Multiplication by delta in O_K on a CM lattice has degree delta conj(delta).
column6: lattice in the complex plane; index of a subgroup
